language_check.method: Script screen only; Latin-script languages are not automatically distinguished from English.

windows.quote:
At the fictional Bell Street Repair Room, a lamp may sit on the shelf waiting for the electrical volunteer while a chair brought in later goes straight to someone who works with wood. Only one volunteer handles electrical faults, and she comes on alternate Saturdays. The workshop has four benches, but an empty one doesn't always mean there's capacity for another job. The work required partly determines the queue; arrival time isn't the only consideration.

Volunteers also need the owner's agreement before buying a replacement part. A repair may be ready to continue and still have to wait for that reply, a pause visitors cannot easily see. The job is unfinished, but that doesn't necessarily mean it's been neglected.

The workshop could make those differences clearer on its status board. Labels such as "waiting for a specialist" and "waiting for your reply" would tell owners more than a single "in progress" column, giving them a better idea of what, if anything, they can do next. Clearer labels wouldn't add volunteer hours or guarantee a completion date.

known_limitations: In the saved 36-document English pilot, high-score false positives occurred on human writing. Do not treat a near-1 score as established authorship.
notes: Four-class model outputs are not proof of authorship or percentages of words.
AI involvement = ai + ai_edited + humanized; human is the mutually exclusive class.
Multi-window document aggregation has not been calibrated; document probability is unavailable.
The model card's threshold at 0.5% FPR is a vendor benchmark setting, not a local guarantee.
Short passages, translations and unfamiliar domains can be unreliable.

occlusion.interpretation: Sensitivity to deleting a paragraph. Positive delta means removal lowered the score; length/context changes confound this. This is not causal authorship evidence or a sentence probability.
